A.subject: Physics
A.text: A car P travelling at 20 ms^(-1) sounds its horn at a frequency of 400 Hz. Another car Q is travelling behind the first car in the same direction with a velocity 40 ms^(-1). The frequency heard by the passenger of the car Q is approximately [Take, velocity of sound = 360 ms^(-1)]
A.sol_text: Using Doppler effect formula for observer (Q) moving towards source (P): f = f0 * (C + v_observer)/(C - v_source) where C = 360 ms^(-1), v_observer = 40 ms^(-1), v_source = 20 ms^(-1), f0 = 400 Hz. Therefore f = 400 * (360 + 40)/(360 - 20) = 400 * (400/340) = 400 * (20/17) ≈ 471 Hz

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A capacitor of capacitance C is charged to a potential V. The flux of the electric field through a closed surface enclosing the positive plate of the capacitor is:
A.sol_text: Using Gauss's law, the electric flux through a closed surface is φ = q_enclosed/ε₀. For a capacitor charged to potential V with capacitance C, the charge on the positive plate is q = CV. Therefore, the flux through a surface enclosing only the positive plate is φ = CV/ε₀.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A bar magnet dropped through a metallic cylindrical pipe takes more time to come down compared to a non-magnetic bar with same geometry and mass. For the magnetic bar, Eddy currents are produced in the metallic pipe which oppose the motion of the magnetic bar. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A.sol_text: Assertion A is true: A magnet falling through a conducting pipe experiences a retarding force due to eddy currents, causing it to fall slower than a non-magnetic object. Reason R is true: Eddy currents induced in the pipe oppose the change in magnetic flux, which opposes the motion of the magnet. R is the correct explanation of A because the eddy currents are the direct cause of the retarding force that makes the magnet fall more slowly.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: When one light ray is reflected from a plane mirror with 30° angle of reflection, the angle of deviation of the ray after reflection is:

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: The logic operations performed by the given digital circuit is equivalent to:
A.sol_text: (A + B).(A.B) = A.(A.B) + B.(A.B) = AB + AB = AB = (AB)' = NOR operation

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If V is the gravitational potential due to sphere of uniform density on it's surface, then it's value at the centre of sphere will be:
A.sol_text: The gravitational potential on the surface of a sphere is V = -GM/R. At the centre of the sphere, using the standard result for gravitational potential inside a uniform sphere: V_centre = -(3/2)(GM/R) = (3/2)V

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In satellite communication, the uplink frequency band used is:
A.sol_text: Uplink frequency band for satellite communication is 5.925 - 6.425 GHz. This is the standard frequency band used for transmitting signals from Earth stations to satellites.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: When vector A = 2i + 3j + 2k is subtracted from vector B, it gives a vector equal to 2j. Then the magnitude of vector B will be:
A.sol_text: Given: B - (2i + 3j + 2k) = 2j. Therefore, B = 2i + 3j + 2k + 2j = 2i + 5j + 2k. Magnitude of B = sqrt(2^2 + 5^2 + 2^2) = sqrt(4 + 25 + 4) = sqrt(33)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A projectile is projected at 30° from horizontal with initial velocity 40 ms^(-1). The velocity of the projectile at t = 2s from the start will be : (Given g = 10 ms^(-2))
A.sol_text:
V_H = 40 cos(30°) = 20sqrt(3) ms^(-1) (horizontal component remains constant)
V_y = 20 - 10 × 2 = 0 ms^(-1) (vertical component at t = 2s)
V = V_H = 20sqrt(3) ms^(-1) (since vertical component is zero at t = 2s)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A body of mass 500 g moves along x-axis such that it's velocity varies with displacement x according to the relation v = 10√x m/s the force acting on the body is:
A.sol_text: Given: v = 10√x, m = 500 g = 0.5 kg. Find dv/dx: dv/dx = 10/(2√x) = 5/√x. Using a = v(dv/dx): a = 10√x × 5/√x = 50 m/s². Using F = ma: F = 0.5 × 50 = 25 N

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency 20 MHz propagates in free space along x-direction. At a particular space and time E = 6.6j v/m. What is B at this point?
A.sol_text: Given E = 6.6j v/m, wave propagates along x-direction. Using E × B = C (Poynting vector direction). Since E is in y-direction and propagation is in x-direction, B must be in z-direction. Using CB₀ = E, where C = 3 × 10^8 m/s. B₀ = E/C = 6.6/(3 × 10^8) = 2.2 × 10^(-8) T. Using right-hand rule for E × B pointing in x-direction: j × B should give x direction, so B is in k direction (positive z).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady of 10 cm/s. If the drops coalesce, the new velocity is
A.sol_text: Using V_T proportional to r^2, where V_T is terminal velocity. For 8 equal drops coalescing: 8r1^3 = r2^3, so r1/r2 = 1/2. Using (V_T)1/(V_T)2 = (r1/r2)^2 = (1/2)^2 = 1/4. Therefore 10/V_T = 1/4, giving V_T = 40 cm/s

A.subject: Physics
A.text: An electron is allowed to move with constant velocity along the axis of current carrying straight solenoid. (A) The electron will experience magnetic force along the axis of the solenoid (B) The electron will not experience magnetic force (C) The electron will continue to move the axis of the solenoid (D) The electron will be accelerated along the axis of the solenoid (E) The electron will follow parabolic path-inside the solenoid
A.sol_text: When an electron moves with constant velocity along the axis of a solenoid, the velocity v is parallel to the magnetic field B inside the solenoid. The Lorentz force is F = q(v × B). Since v is parallel to B, v × B = 0, so F = 0. Therefore, the electron will not experience any magnetic force (B is correct). With no net force, the electron will continue to move along the axis of the solenoid with constant velocity (C is correct). It will not be accelerated (D is incorrect) and will not follow a parabolic path (E is incorrect).

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A space ship of mass 2 × 10^4 kg is launched into a circular orbit close to the earth surface. The additional velocity to be imparted to the space ship in the orbit to overcome the gravitational pull will be (if g = 10 m/s^2 and radius of earth = 6400 km):
A.sol_text: ΔV = sqrt(2GM/R) - sqrt(GM/R) = (sqrt(2) - 1)sqrt(GM/R) = (sqrt(2) - 1)sqrt(gR) = (sqrt(2) - 1)sqrt(10 × 6400 × 10^3) = 8(sqrt(2) - 1) km/s

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
A.text: The ratio of the de-Broglie wavelengths of proton and electron having same kinetic energy : (Assume m_p = m_e × 1849)
A.sol_text: Using de-Broglie wavelength formula λ = h/sqrt(2km). For same kinetic energy K: λ_p/λ_e = sqrt(2k·m_e)/sqrt(2k·m_p) = sqrt(m_e/m_p) = sqrt(1/1849) = 1/43

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The current flowing through R2 is:
A.sol_text: I through battery = 8/2 = 4A. I through CD = (3/9) × 2 = (2/3) A. I through R2 = (1/2) × (2/3) = (1/3) A

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The thermodynamic process, in which internal energy of the system remains constant is
A.sol_text: For internal energy to remain constant, ΔU = 0. From first law of thermodynamics: ΔQ = ΔU + W. If ΔU = 0, then ΔQ = W. This means all heat supplied goes into work done by the system. In an isothermal process, temperature remains constant (ΔT = 0), and for an ideal gas, internal energy depends only on temperature, so ΔU = 0.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If force (F), velocity (V) and time (T) are considered as fundamental physical quantity, then dimensional formula of density will be:
A.sol_text: Density = M/V^3 = ML^-3. Express in terms of F, V, T: F = MLT^-2, so M = FT^2L^-1. V = LT^-1, so L = VT. Therefore M = F(T^2)(V^-1T^-1) = FVT. Density = ML^-3 = (FVT)(VT)^-3 = FVT × V^-3T^-3 = FV^-2T^-2. Simplifying: density dimension = FV^-1T^-2

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A nucleus disintegrates into two nuclear parts, in such a way that ratio of their sizes is 1 : 2^(1/3). Their mass ratio will be
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A metallic cube of side 15 cm moving along y-axis at a uniform velocity of 2 m s^-1. In a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.5 T directed along z-axis. In equilibrium the potential difference between the faces of higher and lower potential developed because of the motion through the field will be .......... mV.
B.sol_text: When a conductor moves through a magnetic field, an EMF is induced. Using the motional EMF formula: EMF = qE = eVB, where V is the velocity, B is the magnetic field, and the effective length is the distance between faces perpendicular to both velocity and field. Here, the cube moves along y-axis with velocity V = 2 m/s, magnetic field B = 0.5 T along z-axis. The EMF develops across the x-axis (perpendicular to both v and B), which has length d = 15 cm = 0.15 m. EMF = VBd = 2 × 0.5 × 0.15 = 0.15 V = 150 mV
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A wire of density 8 × 10^3 kg/m^3 is stretched between two clamps 0.5 m apart. The extension developed in the wire is 3.2 × 10^-4 m. If Y = 8 × 10^10 N/m^2, the fundamental frequency of vibration in the wire will be ...... Hz.
B.sol_text: Using T/μ = Y(ΔL/L) × (1/ρ), where T is tension and μ is mass per unit length. Calculate T/μ = (8×10^10 × 3.2×10^-4 / 0.5) × (1 / 8×10^3) = 6.4×10^3. Then v = sqrt(T/μ) = sqrt(6.4×10^3) = 80 m/s. Fundamental frequency f = v/(2L) = 80/(2×0.5) = 80 Hz.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A coil has an inductance of 2H and resistance of 4Ω. A 10V is applied across the coil. The energy stored in the magnetic field after the current has built up its equilibrium value will be ........ × 10^(-2) J.
B.sol_text: Step 1: At equilibrium, current I = V/R = 10/4 = 5/2 A. Step 2: Energy stored in magnetic field E = (1/2)LI^2 = (1/2) × 2 × (5/2)^2 = 1 × (25/4) = 25/4 = 6.25 J = 625 × 10^(-2) J.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
B.text: A circular plate is rotating in horizontal plane, about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to the plate, with an angular velocity ω. A person sits at the centre having two dumbbells in his hands. When he stretched out his hands, the moment of inertia of the system becomes triple. If E be the initial Kinetic energy of the system, then final Kinetic energy will be E/x. The value of x is
B.sol_text: Using conservation of angular momentum: Iω = I'ω' where I' = 3I. Therefore ω' = ω/3. Initial KE: E = (1/2)Iω^2. Final KE: Ef = (1/2)I'(ω')^2 = (1/2)(3I)(ω/3)^2 = (1/2)(3I)(ω^2/9) = (1/2)Iω^2/3 = E/3. Therefore x = 3.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: For a chemical reaction A + B → Product, the order is 1 with respect to A and B. A table shows: Rate (mol L^-1 S^-1) | [A] (mol L^-1) | [B] (mol L^-1). Row 1: 0.10 | 20 | 0.5. Row 2: 0.40 | x | 0.5. Row 3: 0.80 | 40 | y. What is the value of x and y?
A.sol_text: Since the reaction is first order with respect to both A and B, Rate = k[A][B]. From experiments I and II: [B] is constant (0.5), so comparing rates: 0.40/0.10 = x/20, giving 4 = x/20, so x = 80. From experiments I and III: [A] changes from 20 to 40 (doubles). If rate is first order in A, doubling [A] should double the rate (from 0.10 to 0.20) assuming [B] constant. But rate goes from 0.10 to 0.80 (8 times), so [B] must also increase by 4 times. Since [B] = 0.5 in experiment I, then y = 2 in experiment III would mean [B] doubled, giving 2×4 = 8 times increase. Actually, from 0.40 to 0.80 (double) with [A] constant at 40, [B] must change from 0.5 to y such that doubling occurs, so y = 2 (no change needed as x=80, y=2 satisfies the first order kinetics).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Alkali metal from the following with least melting points is
A.sol_text: From the melting point data provided: Na (371 K), K (336 K), Rb (312 K), Cs (below 312 K based on trend). In alkali metals, melting point decreases as we go down the group from Li to Cs. Therefore, Cs has the least melting point among the given options.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Compound from the following that will not produce precipitate on reaction with AgNO3 is
options: Cyclopropyl bromide (three-membered ring with Br substituent)
A.sol_text: Compounds which result in the formation of stable carbocation upon reacting with AgNO3 will produce precipitate. Compound (4) has Br attached to a sp2 hybridized carbon (alkene), which cannot form a stable carbocation. Compounds (1), (2), and (3) all have Br on sp3 hybridized carbons that can form stable carbocations (primary, secondary, or allylic/benzylic), leading to precipitation of AgBr.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which one of the following pairs is an example of polar molecular solids?
A.sol_text: SO2(s) is a polar molecular solid (bent structure with polar S=O bonds). CO2(s) is non-polar (linear, symmetric). NH3(s) is a polar molecular solid (trigonal pyramidal with lone pair on N). MgO(s) is ionic. HCl(s) is polar molecular but AlN(s) is a covalent solid. Therefore, option (2) SO2(s), NH3(s) contains only polar molecular solids.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which hydride among the following is less stable?
A.sol_text: BeH2 is the least stable among the given hydrides. Hydride stability depends on the strength of the bond between the metal/nonmetal and hydrogen. BeH2 is electron-deficient (beryllium has only 2 valence electrons) and forms only 2 bonds, making it unstable and polymeric. HF is very stable due to high electronegativity difference. NH3 is stable with a complete octet. LiH is ionic and stable. Therefore, BeH2 is the least stable hydride.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: If Ni2+ is replaced by Pt2+ in the complex [NiCl2Br2]2-, which of the following properties are expected to get changed?
options: A. Geometry and D. Magnetic properties
A.sol_text: [NiCl2Br2]2- with Ni2+ is square planar. When Ni2+ is replaced by Pt2+, it remains square planar (geometry unchanged). However, Pt2+ complexes show cis-trans isomerism (geometrical isomerism - B changes). Pt2+ is diamagnetic while Ni2+ is paramagnetic (magnetic properties change - D changes). Optical isomerism (C) does not apply to square planar complexes without chiral centers. Therefore, A (geometry), B (geometrical isomerism), and D (magnetic properties) show changes.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Mg(NH₄)PO₄, B. K₃[Co(NO₂)₆], C. MnO(OH)₂, D. Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃. List II: I. brown, II. white, III. yellow, IV. blue
A.sol_text: Based on known colours of complexes: Mg(NH₄)PO₄ is white (II), K₃[Co(NO₂)₆] is yellow (III), MnO(OH)₂ is brown (I), Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃ is blue (IV). Therefore: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV matches option (2).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the metallurgy process, sulphide ore is converted to oxide before reduction. Statement II: Oxide ores in general are easier to reduce. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
A.sol_text: Statement I is correct: In metallurgy of sulphide ores (like PbS, ZnS, etc.), the ore is first converted to its oxide form through roasting process, then reduced to metal. Statement II is correct: Oxide ores are generally easier to reduce compared to sulphides and other forms because oxides have lower binding energy and reduction is thermodynamically more favorable. Both statements are correct.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A solution is prepared by adding 2 g of X to 1 mole of water. Mass percent of X in the solution is
A.sol_text: Mass percent of X = (mass of X)/(mass of X + mass of water) × 100 = 2/(2 + 18) × 100 = 2/20 × 100 = 10%

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: What weight of glucose must be dissolved in 100 g of water to lower the vapour pressure by 0.20 mm Hg? (Assume dilute solution is being formed). Given: Vapour pressure of pure water is 54.2 mm Hg at room temperature. Molar mass of glucose is 180 g mol^(-1)
A.sol_text: Using the formula (P0 - P)/P = Moles of solute / Moles of solvent. Here P0 = 54.2 mm Hg, P0 - P = 0.20 mm Hg, so P = 54.0 mm Hg. Substituting: (54.2 - 54.0)/54.0 = (w/180)/(100/18). This gives 0.2/54 = (w/180)/(100/18). Solving: w/180 = (0.2/54) × (100/18) = 0.2 × 100/(54 × 18) = 20/972 = 0.0206. Therefore w = 0.0206 × 180 = 3.69 g

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ethane at 333 to 343 K and 6-7 atm pressure in the presence of AlEt3 and TiCl4 undergoes addition polymerization to give LDP. Statement II: Caprolactam at 533-543K in H2O through step growth polymerizes to give Nylon 6. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
A.sol_text: Statement I is FALSE: Ethane undergoes addition polymerization to give HDP (High Density Polyethylene), not LDP. LDP (Low Density Polyethylene) is formed from ethene (ethylene), not ethane. Statement II is TRUE: Caprolactam at 533-543 K in H2O undergoes step growth polymerization to give Nylon 6. This is the correct method for Nylon 6 synthesis.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.sol_text: The reaction sequence shows: Starting material (4-isopropyl phenol) undergoes diazotization with NaNO2/HCl to form intermediate A (diazonium salt with NO group). Treatment of A with NH4SH in H2O leads to reduction of the diazo group (-NO) to amino group (-NH2), giving compound B which is 2-amino-4-isopropyl phenol (structure 1).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: A solution of the product obtained by heating a mole of glycine with a mole of chlorine in presence of red phosphorous generates chiral carbon atom. Reason R: A molecule with 2 chiral carbons is always optically active. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and B are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A.sol_text: Assertion A is true: heating glycine with chlorine in presence of red phosphorous generates a chiral carbon atom (the alpha carbon becomes chiral with Cl, H, NH2, and COOH groups). Reason R is false: A molecule with 2 chiral carbons is not always optically active. For example, a molecule with two chiral carbons can be a meso compound (having internal plane of symmetry) and thus be optically inactive, as shown in the example of the compound with two COOH and two OH groups in the solution.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Assertion A: The given ketone with a chlorine substituent can be subjected to Wolff-Kishner reduction to give the corresponding alkane with chlorine. Reason R: Wolff-Kishner reduction is used to convert C=O into CH2. In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A.sol_text: Assertion A is false because Wolff-Kishner reduction cannot be performed on a molecule containing a chlorine atom directly attached to the carbon bearing the carbonyl group, as the hydrazone intermediate would undergo elimination. Reason R is true - Wolff-Kishner reduction does convert C=O into CH2. Since A is false and R is true, the answer is option (2).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: [CoCl(NH3)5]^2+ absorbs at lower wavelength of light with respect to [Co(NH3)5(H2O)]^3+
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A.sol_text: [CoCl(NH3)5]^2+ absorbs at higher wavelength (not lower) with respect to [Co(NH3)5(H2O)]^3+ because Cl^- is a weaker ligand than H2O. The wavelength of light absorbed depends upon the oxidation state of the metal ion. Since the assertion is false but the reason is true (wavelength does depend on oxidation state), the answer is A is false but R is true.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: H3C - CH2 - CH - CH3 with OH group is treated with (ii) Mg, Dry ether and (iii) D2O to form product [X]. What is product [X]?
options: H3C - CH2 - C - CH3 with H and OH groups
H3C - CH2 - CH - CH3 with D group
A.sol_text: The secondary alcohol H3C-CH2-CH(OH)-CH3 reacts with Mg in dry ether to form a Grignard reagent. The Grignard reagent (R-MgI) is then treated with D2O which acts as a deuterated protic source. The deuterium replaces the hydrogen on the carbon bearing the OH group, yielding H3C-CH2-CH(D)-CH3 as product [X].

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: One mole of P4 reacts with 8 moles of SOCl2 to give 4 moles of A, x mole of SO2 and 2 moles of B. A, B and x respectively are
A.sol_text: P4 + 8SOCl2 → 4PCl3 + 4SO2 + 2S2Cl2. Hence, A = PCl3, x = 4, B = S2Cl2

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The magnetic moment is measured in Bohr Magneton (BM). Spin only magnetic moment of Fe in [Fe(H2O)6]3+ and [Fe(CN)6]3- complexes respectively is:
A.sol_text: [Fe(H2O)6]3+ = d5(H.S.) = 5 unpaired electrons, μ = sqrt(5×7) = sqrt(35) = 5.92 B.M. [Fe(CN)6]3- = d5(L.S.) = 1 unpaired electron, μ = sqrt(1×3) = sqrt(3) = 1.732 B.M.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major product formed in the following reaction is: C6H5 - CH(OH) - CH - CH2 CHO with CH3 substituent, treated with Zn(Hg)/HCl and heat (Δ) to give Major product
options: C6H5 - CH(OH) - CH - C2H5 with CH3 substituent
C6H5 - CH = C - C2H5 with CH3 substituent
C6H5 - C = CH - C2H5 with CH3 substituent
C6H5 with a cyclopentanone ring containing CH3 substituent
A.sol_text: The reaction involves Clemmensen reduction using Zn(Hg)/HCl. The aldehyde group (-CHO) is reduced to -CH3. The OH group is also reduced to -H under these conditions. The double bond is not formed; instead, the aldehyde is converted to methyl group and the secondary alcohol is reduced to CH2. The major product is C6H5 - CH(OH) - CH - C2H5 with CH3 substituent (option A), which represents reduction of the aldehyde to primary alcohol/methyl equivalent.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Number of compounds from the following which will not produce orange red precipitate with Benedict solutions is: Glucose, maltose, sucrose, ribose, 2-deoxyribose, amylose, lactose
B.sol_text: Benedict's test is positive for reducing sugars that have a free or potentially free aldehyde or ketone group. Glucose, maltose, ribose, 2-deoxyribose, and lactose are all reducing sugars and give orange red precipitate. Sucrose is a non-reducing disaccharide (no free aldehyde or ketone group) and amylose is a polysaccharide, neither gives positive Benedict's test. Therefore, 2 compounds (sucrose and amylose) will not produce orange red precipitate.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The maximum number of lone pairs of electron on the central atom from the following species is ........ ClO3-, XeF4, SF4 and I3-
B.sol_text: Analyzing lone pairs on central atom for each species: 1. ClO3-: Cl is central atom with 7 valence electrons, forms 3 bonds with O atoms, has 1 lone pair. 2. XeF4: Xe is central atom with 8 valence electrons, forms 4 bonds with F atoms, has 2 lone pairs. 3. SF4: S is central atom with 6 valence electrons, forms 4 bonds with F atoms, has 1 lone pair. 4. I3-: Central I atom forms 2 bonds, has 3 lone pairs. Maximum lone pairs = 3 (on I3-)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The number of correct statements from the following is ........
B.sol_text: Analyzing each statement: A is correct - 1s orbital has maximum probability density at nucleus. B is incorrect - 2s orbital has a node, probability density first increases, becomes zero at node, then increases again before decreasing. C is incorrect - boundary surface diagrams enclose approximately 90% probability, not 100%. D is correct - p orbitals have 1 angular node, d orbitals have 2 angular nodes. E is correct - p-orbitals have zero probability density at nucleus due to angular node. Therefore, 3 statements (A, D, E) are correct.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: The total number of intensive properties from the following is ........ . Volume, Molar heat capacity, molarity, E° cell, gibbs free energy change, Molar mass, Mole
B.sol_text: Molar heat capacity, molarity, E°cell and molar mass are intensive properties. Volume, gibbs free energy change, and Mole are extensive properties. Therefore, total intensive properties = 4
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: 4.5 moles each of hydrogen and iodine is heated in a sealed ten litre vessel. At equilibrium, 3 moles of HI were found. The equilibrium constant for H2(g) + I2(g) ⇌ 2HI(g) is .........
B.sol_text: Initial moles: H2 = 4.5, I2 = 4.5, HI = 0. At equilibrium: H2 = 3, I2 = 3, HI = 3 (3 moles of HI formed means 1.5 moles each of H2 and I2 reacted). Volume = 10 L. Concentrations: [H2] = 3/10 = 0.3 M, [I2] = 3/10 = 0.3 M, [HI] = 3/10 = 0.3 M. Keq = [HI]^2/([H2][I2]) = (0.3)^2/(0.3 × 0.3) = 0.09/0.09 = 1
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The domain of the function f(x) = 1/sqrt([x]^2 - 3[x] - 10) is (where [x] denotes the greatest integer less or equal to x)
A.sol_text: For domain, [x]^2 - 3[x] - 10 > 0. Factoring: ([x] - 5)([x] + 2) > 0. This gives [x] < -2 or [x] > 5. Since [x] is the greatest integer function, [x] < -2 means [x] ≤ -3 (so x < -2), and [x] > 5 means [x] ≥ 6 (so x ≥ 6). Therefore domain is (-∞, -2) ∪ [6, ∞).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the system of linear equations 7x + 11y + az = 13; 5x + 4y + 7z = β; 175x + 194y + 57z = 361 has infinitely many solutions, then α + β + 2 is equal to
A.sol_text: For a system to have infinitely many solutions, the determinant of coefficients must be zero and all cofactor determinants must also be zero. Setting up the determinant condition: |7 11 α; 5 4 7; 175 194 57| = 0. Using row operations and solving, we get α = -9. Then setting Δ₁ = 0 with |13 11 -9; β 4 7; 361 194 57| = 0, we get β = 11. Therefore, α + β + 2 = -9 + 11 + 2 = 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A = {1, 3, 4, 6, 9} and B = {2, 4, 5, 8, 10}. Let R be a relation defined on A × B such that R = {((a1, b1), (a2, b2)) : a1 ≤ b2 and b1 ≤ a2}. Then the number of elements in the set R is
A.sol_text: For each a1 in A, find valid b2 values in B where a1 ≤ b2. For each b1 in B, find valid a2 values in A where b1 ≤ a2. For a1=1: b2 can be 2,4,5,8,10 (5 values). For a1=3: b2 can be 4,5,8,10 (4 values). For a1=4: b2 can be 4,5,8,10 (4 values). For a1=6: b2 can be 8,10 (2 values). For a1=9: b2 can be 10 (1 value). Total = 5+4+4+2+1 = 16 cases. Similarly for b1 values: b1=2 gives a2 of 3,4,6,9 (4 values), b1=4 gives a2 of 4,6,9 (3 values), b1=5 gives a2 of 6,9 (2 values), b1=8 gives a2 of 9 (1 value), b1=10 gives a2 of none (0 values). Total = 4+3+2+1+0 = 10 cases. Total elements in relation = 16 × 10 = 160

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the mean of 6 observations 1, 2, 4, 5, x and y be 5 and their variance be 10. Then their mean deviation about the mean is equal to
A.sol_text: Given: 6 observations are 1, 2, 4, 5, x, y with mean = 5 and variance = 10. Sum = 1 + 2 + 4 + 5 + x + y = 30, so x + y = 18. Using variance formula: (x^2 + y^2 + 46)/6 - 25 = 10, which gives x^2 + y^2 = 104. Solving x + y = 18 and x^2 + y^2 = 104: x = 10, y = 8. Observations are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 8. Deviations from mean 5: |1-5| = 4, |2-5| = 3, |4-5| = 1, |5-5| = 0, |10-5| = 5, |8-5| = 3. Mean deviation = (4 + 3 + 1 + 0 + 5 + 3)/6 = 16/6 = 8/3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If four distinct points with position vectors a, b, c and d are coplanar, then [a b c] is equal to
options: [d b a]+[a c d]+[d b c]
[a d b]+[d c a]+[d b c]
[d c a]+[b d a]+[c d b]
[b c d]+[d a c]+[d b a]
A.sol_text: Since four points with position vectors a, b, c, d are coplanar: [b-a c-a d-a] = 0. Expanding using the scalar triple product property: (b-a)·((c-a)×(d-a)) = 0. This leads to [b c d]-[b c a]-[b a d]-[a c d] = 0. Therefore: [a b c] = [b c d]+[b a d]+[a c d] = [d c a]+[b d a]+[c d b]

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential equation dy/dx + 5/(x(x^5+1)) * y = (x^5+1)/x^7, x > 0. If y(1) = 2, then y(2) is equal to
A.sol_text: This is a linear differential equation of the form dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x). The integrating factor is I.F. = e^(∫ 5/(x(x^5+1)) dx). Using substitution 1/x^5 + 1 = t, we get I.F. = x^5/(1+x^5). Multiplying both sides by I.F. and solving: y(x^5/(1+x^5)) = ∫ (x^5(1+x^5)^2)/(1+x^5) * 1/x^7 dx + c = -1/x + x^3/4 + c. Using initial condition y(1) = 2: 2(1/2) = -1 + 1/4 + c, so c = 7/4. At x = 2: y(32/33) = -1/2 + 2 + 7/4 = 693/128. Therefore y(2) = 693/128.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let P be the plane passing through the points (5, 3, 0), (13, 3, -2) and (1, 6, 2). For a ∈ N, if the distances of the points A(3, 4, a) and B(2, a, a) from the plane P are 2 and 3 respectively, then the positive value of a is
A.sol_text: Find vectors AB and AC from the three given points. Calculate normal vector using AB × AC = 6i - 8j + 24k. Equation of plane: 6x - 8y + 24z = 6, simplified to 3x - 4y + 12z = 3. Distance of A(3, 4, a) from plane = |9 - 16 + 12a - 3|/sqrt(9 + 16 + 144) = |12a - 10|/13 = 2, giving a = 3. Distance of B(2, a, a) from plane = |6 - 4a + 12a - 3|/13 = |8a + 3|/13 = 3, giving 8a + 3 = 39, so a = 4.5 or 8a - 9 = 39, giving a = 6 or a = 4. Since a ∈ N and both conditions must be satisfied, a = 4.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the function f: [0, 2] → R be defined as f(x) = {e^(min(x^2,x)), x ∈ [0, 1); e^(x-log x), x ∈ [1, 2]}. Where [t] denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to t. Then the value of the integral ∫₀² xf(x) dx is
A.sol_text: For x ∈ [0, 1): min(x^2, x) = x^2, so f(x) = e^(x^2). For x ∈ [1, 2]: x - ln x ∈ [1, 2), so [x - ln x] = 1, thus f(x) = e. ∫₀² xf(x) dx = ∫₀¹ x·e^(x^2) dx + ∫₁² x·e dx. For first integral, use substitution u = x^2, du = 2x dx: (1/2)∫₀¹ e^u du = (1/2)(e - 1). For second integral: e·[x^2/2]₁² = e(2 - 1/2) = 3e/2. Total = (e-1)/2 + 3e/2 = 2e - 1/2

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If f: R → R be a continuous function satisfying ∫[0 to π/2] f(sin 2x) sin x dx + α ∫[0 to π/4] f(cos 2x) cos x dx = 0, then the value of α is
A.sol_text: Let I = ∫[0 to π/2] f(sin 2x) sin x dx. Split this as ∫[0 to π/4] + ∫[π/4 to π/2]. In the second integral, substitute x = π/2 - u to get ∫[0 to π/4] f(cos 2x)(1/sqrt(2) cos x - 1/sqrt(2) sin x) dx + ∫[0 to π/4] f(cos 2x)(1/sqrt(2) cos x + 1/sqrt(2) sin x) dx = ∫[0 to π/4] f(cos 2x)(sqrt(2) cos x) dx. For the given equation to hold, α = -sqrt(2).

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the radius of the largest circle with centre (2, 0) inscribed in the ellipse x^2 + 4y^2 = 36 is r, then 12r^2 is equal to
A.sol_text: Equation of normal at P(6 cos θ, 3 sin θ) is 6 sec θ x - 3 cosec θ y = 27. If it passes through (2, 0), then 12 sec θ = 27, so cos θ = 4/9 and sin θ = sqrt(65)/9. Point P is (8/3, sqrt(65)/3). Radius r = OP = sqrt((8/3 - 2)^2 + (sqrt(65)/3)^2) = sqrt((2/3)^2 + 65/9) = sqrt(69/9) = sqrt(69)/3. Therefore, 12r^2 = 12 × 69/9 = 92.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let the line passing through the points P(2, -1, 2) and Q(5, 3, 4) meet the plane x - y + z = 4 at the point R. Then the distance of the point R from the plane x + 2y + 3z + 2 = 0 measured parallel to the line (x-7)/2 = (y+3)/2 = (z-2)/1 is
A.sol_text: Equation of line PQ: (x-2)/3 = (y+1)/4 = (z-2)/2 = λ. Let R be (3λ+2, 4λ-1, 2λ+2). R lies on plane x - y + z = 4, so 3λ + 2 - 4λ + 1 + 2λ + 2 = 4, giving λ = -1. Thus R(-1, -5, 0). Let SR be the given line: (x+1)/2 = (y+5)/2 = z/1 = k. S(2k-1, 2k-5, k) lies on plane x + 2y + 3z + 2 = 0, so (2k-1) + 2(2k-5) + 3k + 2 = 0, giving 9k - 9 = 0, so k = 1. Thus S(1, -3, 1). SR = sqrt(4 + 4 + 1) = 3

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the determinant |x, x+λ, x| |x, x, x+λ²| = (9/8)(103x + 81), then λ, λ/3 are the roots of the equation
A.sol_text: Expanding the determinant by putting x = 0 gives λ^3 = (3^6)/(2^3), so λ = 9/2. Then λ/3 = 3/2. Using sum of roots = 9/2 + 3/2 = 6 and product = (9/2)(3/2) = 27/4, the equation is x^2 - 6x + 27/4 = 0, which simplifies to 4x^2 - 24x + 27 = 0.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the letters of the word MATHS are permuted and all possible words so formed are arranged as in a dictionary with serial numbers, then the serial number of the word THAMS is
A.sol_text: To find the rank of THAMS: Compare each position with letters that come before it alphabetically in the remaining letters. T is 2nd, H is 1st, A is 1st, M is 1st, S is 1st in their respective positions. Rank = 4! + 4! + 1×3! + 1 = 96 + 6 + 1 = 103

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a, b, c and d be positive real numbers such that a + b + c + d = 11. If the maximum value of a^5*b^3*c^2*d is 3750*beta, then the value of beta is
A.sol_text: Using AM-GM inequality, assume the numbers in the ratio a/5 : a/5 : a/5 : a/5 : b/3 : b/3 : b/3 : c/2 : c/2 : d. Apply AM >= GM on these 11 terms. The sum equals 11. At equality, a^5*b^3*c^2*d <= 90 × 3750, so a^5*b^3*c^2*d_max = 90 × 3750. Therefore beta = 90.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: For a ∈ C, let A = {z ∈ C : Re(a + z̄) > Im(ā + z)}; B = {z ∈ C : Re(a + z̄) < Im(ā + z)}. Then among the two statements: (S1) If Re(a), Im(a) > 0, then the set A contains all the real numbers (S2) If Re(a), Im(a) < 0, then the set B contains all the real numbers
A.sol_text: Let a = x₁ + iy₁, ā = x₁ - iy₁, z = x₂ + iy₂, z̄ = x₂ - iy₂. Then A = {z : x₁ + x₂ > y₂ - y₁} = {z : x₁ + y₁ + x₂ > y₂}. B = {z : x₁ + x₂ < y₂ - y₁} = {z : x₁ + y₁ + x₂ < y₂}. For S1: If y₂ = 0 and x₁, y₁ > 0, then A requires x₂ > -(x₁ + y₁), which does not cover the whole real axis. For S2: If y₂ = 0 and x₁, y₁ < 0, then B requires x₂ < -(x₁ + y₁), which does not cover the whole real axis. Therefore, both statements are false.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The sum of the coefficients of three consecutive terms in the binomial expansion of (1 + x)^(n+2), which are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5, is equal to
A.sol_text: Let the three consecutive terms be T_r, T_(r+1), T_(r+2). Given ratio 1:3:5. Using T_(r+1)/T_r = (n+2-r+1)/(r) = 3, we get n - 4r + 3 = 0 ... (1). Using T_(r+2)/T_(r+1) = (n+2-(r+1)+1)/(r+1) = 5/3, we get 3n - 8r + 1 = 0 ... (2). Solving (1) and (2): n = 5, r = 2. The coefficients are C(7,2) + C(7,3) + C(7,4) = 21 + 35 + 35 = 91. Wait, recalculating: 7 + 21 + 35 = 63.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The angle of elevation of the top P of a tower from the feet of one person standing due south of the tower is 45° and from the feet of another person standing due west of the tower is 30°. If the height of the tower is 5 meters, then the distance (in meters) between the two persons is equal to
A.sol_text: Let A be the base of the tower and P be the top. Let B be the person to the west and another person to the south. Height of tower PA = 5 m. From angle of elevation 45° (south): tan(45°) = 5/x₁, so x₁ = 5. From angle of elevation 30° (west): tan(30°) = 5/x₂, so x₂ = 5*sqrt(3). Since the two persons are positioned due south and due west from the tower base, they form a right angle at A. Using Pythagorean theorem: AB = sqrt(x₁² + x₂²) = sqrt(25 + 75) = sqrt(100) = 10 meters.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The number of points, where the curve f(x) = e^8x - e^6x - 3e^4x - e^2x + 1, x ∈ R cuts x-axis is equal to
B.sol_text: f(x) = e^8x - e^6x - 3e^4x - e^2x + 1. As x → -∞, lim f(x) = 1, and f(0) = -3, lim f(x) → ∞ as x → +∞. Since f(0) = -3 < 0, f(x) is continuous, and the limits show one root is negative and another is positive. Therefore, the curve cuts the x-axis at exactly 2 points.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let S = {z ∈ C - {i, 2i} : (z + 8iz - 15)/(z^2 - 3iz - 2) ∈ R}. If α - (13/11)i ∈ S, α ∈ R - {0}, then 242α^2 is equal to
B.sol_text: Put z = x + iy. For the expression (z^2 + 8iz - 15)/(z^2 - 3iz - 2) to be real, its imaginary part must be zero. Expanding and simplifying the condition leads to (11x^2 + 11y^2 + 26y - 61 = 0). Since α ≠ 0, we get x = 0 (neglected case gives x = 0). Substituting y = -13/11 and x = α into the equation: 11α^2 + 11(169/121) - 26(13/11) - 61 = 0. Solving: 121α^2 = 840, therefore 242α^2 = 1680.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.text: Let the probability of getting head for a biased coin be 1/4. It is tossed repeatedly until a head appears. Let N be the number of tosses required. If the probability that the equation 64x^2 + 5Nx + 1 = 0 has no real root is p/q, where p and q are co-prime, then q - p is equal to .........

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: If A is the area in the first quadrant enclosed by the curve C: 2x^2 - y + 1 = 0, the tangent to C at the point (1, 3) and the line x + y = 1, then the value of 60A is ......
B.sol_text: From curve C: 2x^2 - y + 1 = 0, we get y = 2x^2 + 1. Finding tangent at (1, 3): dy/dx = 4x, so at x = 1, slope = 4. Tangent equation: y - 3 = 4(x - 1), giving y = 4x - 1. Find intersection of tangent y = 4x - 1 and line x + y = 1: x + 4x - 1 = 1, so x = 2/5, y = 3/5. Intersection of curve y = 2x^2 + 1 and line x + y = 1: x + 2x^2 + 1 = 1, so x = 0, giving point (0, 1). Required area = (1/2) × (1/2) × (2/5) + integral from 0 to 3 of [(y+1)/4 - (y-1)^(1/2)/2] dy = 4/15. Therefore 60A = 60 × (4/15) = 16.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let the tangent to the parabola y^2 = 12x at the point (3, α) be perpendicular to the line 2x + 2y = 3. Then the square of distance of the point (6, -4) from the normal to the hyperbola α^2*x^2 - 9y^2 = 9α^2 at its point (α - 1, α + 2) is equal to ........
B.sol_text: From y^2 = 12x, slope of tangent at (3, α) is 6/α. Given tangent perpendicular to 2x + 2y = 3 (slope -1), so 6/α = 1, thus α = 6. Hyperbola: 36x^2 - 9y^2 = 324 or x^2/9 - y^2/36 = 1. Normal at (5, 8): 5x - 2y = 9. Distance from (6, -4) to normal = |30 + 8 - 9|/sqrt(29) = 29/sqrt(29) = sqrt(29). Square of distance = 116.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer correct to two decimal places.
